target.title: fix(scripts): gh-read stops hanging on stalled GitHub CLI commands
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where maintainers and repository automation using `scripts/gh-read` could hang indefinitely when the delegated GitHub CLI process stopped responding. A stalled read command could therefore block the surrounding workflow without returning an actionable failure.

## Why This Change Was Made

The wrapper now applies the established two-minute GitHub script budget to delegated `gh` commands and uses `SIGKILL` when that deadline expires. The execution seam remains synchronous, preserves the installation token environment and inherited stdio, and propagates the original spawn error to the caller.

## User Impact

`scripts/gh-read` now exits with an `ETIMEDOUT` error instead of hanging forever when GitHub CLI commands stall. Successful commands and normal nonzero exit statuses keep their existing behavior.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/gh-read.test.ts` — 16/16 passed.
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 scripts/gh-read.ts test/scripts/gh-read.test.ts` — passed.
- Targeted Oxlint for `scripts/gh-read.ts` — passed.
- Real Node subprocess proof returned `ETIMEDOUT`, `SIGKILL`, and a null status for a deliberately stalled child.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- The scripts and root-test TypeScript lanes were attempted locally but the installed dependency snapshot lacks two `@openclaw/fs-safe/advanced` exports required by unchanged `src/infra/boundary-file-read.ts`; the reported files match `origin/main` and are outside this patch.
